extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, agents, attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing, examining, and granting corrections to U.S. patents (reissue applications, certificates of correction, disclaimers) under 35 U.S.C. 251, 255, 256 and related regulations; includes procedural and substantive criteria examiners and applicants must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed mechanisms for correcting patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be corrected or amended in four ways: (A) by reissue, (B) by the issuance of a certificate of correction which becomes a part of the patent, (C) by disclaimer, and (D) by reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This chapter discusses the first three mechanisms; reexamination is covered elsewhere (MPEP Chapter 2200). Use the appropriate statutory/regulatory route depending on the nature of the error and the remedy sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory grounds for reissue (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue is available 'whenever any patent is, through error without any deceptive intention, deemed wholly or partly inoperative or invalid, by reason of a defective specification or drawing, or by reason of the patentee claiming more or less than he had a right to claim in the patent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue requires surrender of the patent and payment of the fee; no new matter may be introduced; Commissioner may issue multiple reissues for distinct parts; application provisions apply except that assignee may make/swear application if it does not seek to enlarge claims. Reissue enlarging claims must be applied for within two years of grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes an 'error' supporting reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: An error arises from conduct during preparation/prosecution of the application that caused the patent to be deemed wholly or partly inoperative or invalid under 35 U.S.C. 251; mere spelling/grammar/typographical/editorial/clerical corrections that do not cause such inoperativeness do not justify reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common bases: (A) claims too narrow or too broad; (B) disclosure inaccuracies; (C) failure to or incorrect claiming of foreign priority; (D) failure to reference or incorrect reference to copending applications. Case law examples (e.g., In re Wilder, Ex parte Scudder) illustrate when reissue applies (e.g., attorney's failure to appreciate scope, misjoinder corrections). Some failures (e.g., failure to timely file divisional) are not correctable by reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence/timing rule for broadening reissue claims (two-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: No reissued patent shall be granted enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent unless applied for within two years from the grant of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a broadening reissue is filed within two years, diligence is presumed and the examiner should not normally reject for delay. A filing on the two-year anniversary is considered within two years. See MPEP § 1412.03 for practice on broadening reissue claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for submissions when reissue patent is in litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers for reissue applications involved in litigation should be marked 'REISSUE LITIGATION' on the outside envelope and the top right-hand portion of the papers and identified with the relevant PTO unit to obtain expedited handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protestor participation is limited per 37 CFR 1.291(c). Markings should be prominent (bright color) and such papers receive special attention. See MPEP § 1442.01–§ 1442.04 for examination of litigation-related reissue applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in a reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application must contain the same parts required for an original patent application, complying with all applicable rules, and additionally must satisfy reissue-specific requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reissue specification (including claims and drawings) should be the copy of the patent submitted; a reissue oath/declaration complying with 37 CFR 1.63 and 1.175 is required; where patent is assigned, written consent of all assignees and evidence of ownership are required; an offer to surrender the original patent is recommended (required before allowance); priority claims (35 U.S.C. 119/120) and IDS may be filed. Missing parts (oath/fee/assignee consent) may be supplied later under 37 CFR 1.53(f) with surcharge if applicable. Use Box REISSUE for expedited initial filings only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration and assignee consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath/declaration must be signed by the inventor(s) unless otherwise provided; written consent of all assignees owning an undivided interest is required, except an assignee of the entire interest may make the oath if no enlargement of claims is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee consent must establish ownership under 37 CFR 3.73(b) either by documentary chain of title filed in the reissue application or by specifying where such evidence is recorded in the Office (e.g., reel/frame). The consent and ownership submission must be signed by a party authorized to act for the assignee. If assignee consent cannot be obtained, a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 may be filed for waiver; application may receive a filing date without the oath/consent but will get a missing parts notice and may accrue surcharge obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof and form of establishing assignee ownership (37 CFR 3.73(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership is established by (A) filing documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee (e.g., executed assignment), or (B) specifying where such evidence is recorded in the Office (reel/frame).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission must be signed by a party authorized to act for the assignee (attorney signature alone is insufficient unless so authorized). If the signature is by a non-recognized officer, acceptance is possible if the record includes a statement empowering that person to sign; examiners should compare the consenting assignee and the documentary evidence to ensure they match. Use form paragraphs 14.16 et seq. to object where ownership proof is lacking or improperly signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of specification in a reissue application (formatting rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire specification and claims of the patent must be included, with matter to be omitted enclosed in square brackets and additions underlined; claims should not be renumbered and numbering of new claims should follow the highest numbered patent claim. No new matter may be introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut-up soft copies of the original patent (single column mounted separately) are recommended for preparing the reissue specification; however, amendments after filing must follow 37 CFR 1.121(b). For twice reissued patents, use double underlining and double bracketing; printed patents may use bold face and double bracketing. Entire words or chemical formulas must be shown as changed — partial-word changes are not permitted. Charts/tables/formulas spanning columns should not be split but provided in entirety and may extend beyond the column width.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of prior Certificates of Correction and disclaimers in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes made by a Certificate of Correction or a disclaimer in the original patent should be included in the reissue application without underlining or bracketting (they are considered part of the original patent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Certificate of Correction changes are extensive or were improperly filed with underlining/brackets, the examiner may request a clean copy of the specification including those corrections so that they appear as part of the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new matter in reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: New matter (matter not present in the patent sought to be reissued) is excluded from a reissue application under 35 U.S.C. 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in the reissue must be for subject matter the applicant had the right to claim in the original patent; omissions (e.g., omitted feature or step in method) can create new matter. If new matter is added anywhere, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 251 should be made (form paragraph 14.22.01). If new matter affects claims, also consider a 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph rejection; if it doesn't affect claims, an objection under 35 U.S.C. 132 may be appropriate (form paragraph 7.28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue claims must be for the same general invention as the original patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue claims must be for the same invention disclosed as being the invention in the original patent; the entire disclosure (not just claims) is considered to determine the patentee's objective intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proper test is an objective inquiry confined to the intent manifested by the original patent (In re Amos). Reissue claims will satisfy 35 U.S.C. 251 where (A) they are described and enabled by the original specification such that 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph is satisfied, and (B) nothing in the original specification indicates an intent not to claim the subject matter. Explicit statements in the original spec that an embodiment is unsuitable can bar reissue claims to it; mere failure to claim a disclosed embodiment is usually not fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture rule (prohibition on recapturing surrendered subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue will not be granted to 'recapture' claimed subject matter that was surrendered in the original prosecution to obtain allowance of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the two-step Clement/Mentor test: (1) determine in what aspects the reissue claims are broader than the patent claims (e.g., omission of a limitation), and (2) determine whether those broader aspects relate to subject matter formerly surrendered (look to prosecution history for arguments/changes made to overcome prior art or objections). If limitations omitted were presented/argued/stated to obtain allowance, recapture exists and is impermissible. Examiners must review prosecution history of the original file to determine surrender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination standard for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application is examined in the same manner as an original application, including review of reissue oath/declaration, claims for broadening or new matter, and issues of fraud/inequitable conduct or duty of disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial examiner review should inspect for required submissions (oath, assignee consent, proof of ownership). Rejections and actions (including protests, interference considerations, and stays in litigation-related cases) should follow existing examination practice; various form paragraphs (e.g., 14.15–14.22) exist for common deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative correction mechanism for inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: If the only change is correction of inventorship, this can be accomplished by filing a request for a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 256 and 37 CFR 1.324 instead of reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Certificate of Correction will be issued if all parties are in agreement and the inventorship issue is not contested. See MPEP § 1412.04 and § 1481.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee signature capacity and acceptable evidence when not a recognized officer
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission establishing ownership or a consent must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee; where signed by a non-recognized officer, acceptance is possible if the record contains a statement empowering that person to sign or a separate empowerment statement is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 14.16.02–14.16.06 guide examiners in objecting when capacity is not stated, when the signer lacks capacity, or when an attorney/agent of record improperly signed. A new submission including an empowerment statement or separate paper referencing prior submission with proper empowerment will be acceptable. Examiner should require signature by an authorized party; attorney signature alone is insufficient unless that person is authorized.
